column2: Revision_Deflation_CJT_and_Kohn-Sham_definition_C: checks of superfluid dark matter on the deflating spacetime

column4: superfluid dark matter without deflation: the copy of the Einstein-Boltzmann program reproduces the files data/sfdm_summary.csv and data/sfdm_bounds.csv of the main project (half-mode wavenumbers of 15 models; limits on the fermion mass and on the sound speed of a condensate) to the digits written there (largest relative deviations 3.4e-11 and 3.1e-11)

superfluid dark matter on the deflating spacetime (data/sfdm_deflation_summary.csv, sfdm_deflation_bounds.csv). The wavenumber below which the first sound of the fluid suppresses structure (half-mode) changes by -0.164 to -0.149 per cent at the rate that lunar laser ranging allows and by -3.28 to -3.04 per cent at the rate that nucleosynthesis allows (15 models; each background at the Hubble constant that keeps the angle theta_*). The limits that follow from the Lyman-alpha bound on thermal warm dark matter of 5.3 keV move from m > 1.514 keV (fermions, weak pairing) and c_s0 < 1.645e-11 c (condensate; Thomas-Fermi radius < 0.365 pc) without deflation to m > 1.516 keV, c_s0 < 1.641e-11 c (0.364 pc) at the rate of lunar laser ranging and m > 1.555 keV, c_s0 < 1.565e-11 c (0.347 pc) at the rate of nucleosynthesis. The suppression is set while the fluid still has pressure, long before today, when gravity was weaker: the Jeans wavenumber is proportional to the square root of Newton's constant, which in the early universe was 0.9969 and 0.9383 of today's value at the two rates (square root minus one: -0.154 and -3.13 per cent). The two closures give the same half-mode wavenumbers to 1.5e-5
